question: What will the first reported revenues after September 2026 be for the following companies? (AMD)

calls.reasoning: Prior: AMD's Q3 2026 guide is $13.0B +/- $0.3B; consensus is about $13.08-13.12B. Reference class: AMD's last six quarters beat the guidance midpoint by +4.8%, +3.9%, +6.3%, +7.0%, +4.6% and +3.0% (mean ~4.9%), which applied to $13.0B gives about $13.39-13.91B. I shaded the median down to ~$13.49B (+3.8%) because the most recent beat was the smallest, there is stress in AI-infrastructure credit, and AMD guided to a significant double-digit decline in Gaming. Upside: an unverified search snippet says Polymarket prices a 62% chance that data-center revenue tops $8B (vs $6.7B in Q2). No market on total revenue was found on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold. Small tail above $14.2B.

- AMD Q2 2026 8-K/press release (Aug 4, 2026): Q2 revenue $11.536B, +50% y/y; Data Center ~$6.7B (58% of revenue, doubled y/y). Q3 2026 outlook: ~$13.0B +/- $0.3B (+41% y/y, +13% q/q), non-GAAP gross margin ~56%. Segment outlook: Data Center up strong double digits, Embedded up strong double digits, Client+Gaming down (Client growth more than offset by a significant double-digit Gaming decline).
- Q2 2026 guide was ~$11.2B +/- $0.3B; actual $11.536B, +3.0% vs midpoint (Shacknews / search results, Aug 2026). Consensus for Q2 had been $11.31B.
- Beats vs guidance midpoint, from the question's revenue history and recalled prior guides (recalled guides not re-verified this run): Q1'25 guide $7.1B -> $7.438B (+4.8%); Q2'25 $7.4B -> $7.685B (+3.9%); Q3'25 $8.7B -> $9.246B (+6.3%); Q4'25 $9.6B -> $10.270B (+7.0%); Q1'26 $9.8B -> $10.253B (+4.6%); Q2'26 $11.2B -> $11.536B (+3.0%). Range +3.0% to +7.0% over 6 quarters; the most recent is the lowest.
- Consensus Q3 2026 revenue: MarketBeat $13.09B; Zacks $13.12B; Cryptobriefing ~$13.08B (late Oct / early Nov 2026). Reported streak of 15 straight quarterly revenue beats vs consensus.
- Bearish context (Cryptobriefing, ~Nov 1, 2026): stress in AI-infrastructure credit (one borrower's 2032 notes at 15% yield, CDS spreads nearly doubled in October), IREN down 60% y/y, Anthropic IPO filing showing a large loss; the risk named is data-center operators slowing builds. FX Leaders (Oct 31): stock testing ~$502 support.
- Bullish context: a search snippet (source unclear) cites a Polymarket contract on Q3 Data Center revenue > $8B (vs $6.7B in Q2). Its price is withheld here to avoid anchoring.
- Status quo: AMD lands inside its guidance range or above it; it has not missed the guidance midpoint in recent years.
- Resolves off AMD's Q3 FY2026 earnings release/8-K total revenue (initial figure), not segment revenue or later restatements.
- Event window: release expected Nov 3, 2026 after market close; as of Nov 2, 2026 22:30 UTC it has not been reported (about 1 day remaining).
- Searched, not found: any Kalshi or Manifold market on AMD total revenue; any buy-side whisper number for revenue; any pre-announcement.

calls.reasoning: AMD guided Q3 2026 to ~$13.0B ± $0.3B; consensus ~$13.06-13.12B; Jefferies $13.5B. AMD beat its guide midpoint in all of the last 8 quarters by +1.8% to +7.0% (mean ~4.2%), which implies ~$13.5B. Shaded slightly below the mean for the smallest recent beat (Q2'26 +3.0%), supply tightness, gaming decline and AI-infra credit stress; Data Center momentum supports the beat. No human prediction market on total revenue found (none on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold per runs). Escape beyond $12.0B/$14.2B would need an ~8% miss or ~9% beat, unprecedented recently.
calls.reconciliation: All runs agree on guide ($13.0B±0.3B), consensus (~$13.06-13.12B), and the resolution source (initial 8-K revenue, Nov 3 2026). Main factual dispute: Run 1 used a 6-quarter beat history (mean 4.9%) and left out Q3'24/Q4'24 (+1.8%/+2.1%), which Runs 2 and 3 cite; those guides ($6.7B, $7.5B) match my recollection, so I used the 8-quarter set (mean ~4.2%), not verified by web this run. Judgment: how much to shade for supply limits, gaming and AI-capex credit stress versus Data Center strength and the 15-quarter consensus-beat streak; I took a median of ~+3.7% over the midpoint, close to Jefferies' $13.5B. The unverified Polymarket Data Center snippet in Run 1 is a different quantity and I did not weight it. No escape mass: there is no recent precedent for an 8% miss or 9% beat. I retrieved nothing myself.
